memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If it had not turned away, I would certainly have killed you by now, but I would have spared it." Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not realise you were standing in the road to oppose me. Now if you are displeased, I will go back." - Num 22:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The angel reveals just how close Balaam came to death. Three times the donkey turned aside, and three times it spared his life. The very animal he beat in fury had been the instrument of God's mercy toward him. Without that lowly donkey, Balaam would already be dead.

Faced with this truth, Balaam confesses, "I have sinned." He admits he did not perceive the Lord's opposition. And he offers to turn back if God is displeased. It sounds like repentance, though as the story continues we will see that his heart is still not fully surrendered. Even so, in this moment he acknowledges his wrong.

The scene overflows with unrecognised mercy. How often has God protected us from dangers we never saw? How many times have unseen hands turned us aside from harm we did not even know was there? We are surrounded by mercies we fail to notice, spared by grace we never thank Him for.

Take a moment to consider the mercies you have missed. The near-misses, the closed doors, the delays that kept you from disaster: these may well be God's protecting hand. In Christ we live under mercy every single day (Lam 3:22-23). Let gratitude replace the grumbling of a heart that only sees its frustrations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What unseen mercies has God shown you that you may have overlooked?
2. Do you thank God for the dangers He has spared you from?
3. How does recognising God's protection change your outlook today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Merciful Father, thank You for the countless dangers You have spared me from without my even knowing. Open my eyes to Your daily mercies and fill my heart with gratitude. Amen.
